sources.entry: Nightwatch - Menu-bar app for amateur astronomers that says when tonight will be clear enough for a long imaging session, and what to point at.

summary.one_liner: Nightwatch is a free macOS menu-bar app for amateur astrophotographers that finds tonight's clear imaging window, ranks targets for it, and says when to set up.
summary.what_it_does: It fetches cloud, rain chance, dew point, wind and visibility for your site (from Apple Weather when signed for it, otherwise Open-Meteo), plus seeing and transparency from 7Timer and aerosol forecasts from Open-Meteo's air-quality service. It computes darkness, Moon, planets and target visibility locally with Astronomy Engine and applies a user-set go rule (default: 3 h clear run, cloud at or under 25%, targets above 30°). Menu-bar icon, popover sky score, and alerts before and when the clear window opens are driven by that rule. The target browser groups objects visible during the window with DSS2 thumbnails, per-card timelines and field-of-view fit, plus a Tonight's plan page, a week-ahead view, and Events (meteor showers, eclipses, ISS passes, lunar occultations). Users can mark their own horizon by direction (manually or from a phone photo) so targets behind houses or trees are excluded. It also suggests dark-sky sites from bundled certified-site lists and light-pollution grids, and has optional aurora alerts, desktop widgets, Spotlight and Shortcuts actions, and iCloud settings sync.
use_cases: check when tonight's sky is clear enough for astrophotography
plan which targets to image on a clear night
find dark sky sites near home
get alerts when the clear window opens
plan a week of astrophotography sessions
check whether a meteor shower, eclipse or ISS pass is visible tonight
work out which targets are blocked by trees or houses
how_to_run: scripts/fetch-data.sh (optional, only to refresh the bundled catalogue)
scripts/build-app.sh (builds with Xcode, signs ad hoc, installs to /Applications, launches)
notable: Horizon mapping: set how high houses, trees or hills block the sky per compass direction, or measure from a phone photo, and all target times follow it
Tonight's plan with favourites, suggestions to fill gaps, and per-night choices synced across Macs
Dark-site finder using bundled light-pollution grids, with suggested dark car parks found from Apple Maps data
Bright-nights mode suggests the Moon and naked-eye planets when true darkness never arrives in summer at British latitudes
Accessibility work: VoiceOver descriptions, Reduce Transparency and Increase Contrast support, adjustable text size
caveats: Requires macOS 14 or later and Apple silicon for the published download; building from source needs Xcode 26 or later and xcodegen.
Apple Weather use requires an Apple Developer signing setup tied to the maintainer's team; other builds fall back to Open-Meteo.
Desktop widget and its helper only work in a signed build; ad hoc builds omit the widget.
